title: Report how long stages, tests, bug fixes and human decisions took, from existing records
description: Report how long stages, tests, bug fixes and human decisions took, from existing records
acceptance_criteria: `chough timing` (text, and `--json`) reports each stage visit as a segment with start, end and elapsed wall-clock time derived from `.chough/transitions.jsonl`: each advance, iterate, back, reset, skip, pause, resume, side-stage enter and return record ends the open segment and starts the next, while `gate-opened` and `gate-closed` records neither start nor end a segment; iterations and side-stage visits are counted separately, and paused time is shown on its own and excluded from active time. Every `reset`, whatever its destination, starts a new cycle and `back` never does; the first cycle starts at the first record, and the segment before it is shown with an unknown start because init and migrate write no transition. Time in `done` until the next reset is reported as idle between cycles and is excluded from stage time and from estimates (LIFE-10, REQ-cli-020).

`chough checkpoint --awaiting-human "<gate>"` appends one `gate-opened` transition (kind, current stage, gate text, time, revision) only when that gate is not already open, and `--clear-awaiting-human` appends one `gate-closed` transition per gate it clears, in the same command that already writes the checkpoint. The report shows each gate's open, close and waiting time, gates still open as open with elapsed-so-far, and per stage active time separately from waiting-on-human time. Gate records are reconciled with the checkpoint's current awaiting-human list: a gate opened in transitions, never closed there and no longer in the list is reported closed at an unknown time, and a gate in the list without a `gate-opened` record, such as one opened before this change, has an unknown open time. The record says only when a gate was opened and cleared; it never records or implies who decided or what was decided (LIFE-10, REQ-cli-020, REQ-cli-007, REQ-cli-008).

Tests and bug fixes: per case and environment the report lists observation times and outcomes and, for validation runs, their recorded attempts and total run wall-clock time (`elapsed_seconds`, which includes interval waits and resumes and is labelled so, not as per-test time); per bug it shows created, reproduced (the earliest linked failed observation, using the retention ledger's recorded time for a pruned one, and unknown with reason unavailable when any linked observation is neither present nor in the ledger), verified (the first note whose recorded changes include `status: <old> -> verified`), and the elapsed time between them. Durations no record holds, such as a single case run's run time today, are reported unknown, never zero (LIFE-10, REQ-cli-020).

Native lifecycle times are taken only from native SpecSync output or native records read read-only (change created and updated from `specsync change status --json`; definition approval, verification, review and finalization as resolved by the open native-source question). From native approval records only the gate, timestamp and reopening timestamps are read, never the actor, note or any other field; approval validity comes only from `change status`, and an approval that status reports invalid, or that a later reopening superseded, is reported as reopened or not current, never as a current approval. The current change takes one bounded status read; history across archived changes takes one bounded read per archived change for at most the 10 most recent, and older ones are reported partial with the count skipped. A time native output does not expose, an unavailable, failed, oversized or timed-out native read, or an unrecognised record shape is shown unknown with its reason; Chough copies no native state into its own records (LIFE-10, LIFE-6, REQ-cli-003, REQ-cli-020).

Honest labels: every duration is labelled elapsed wall-clock time, not effort; history summaries show the sample count with minimum, median and maximum, labelled an estimate from recorded history and not a target, and fewer than 3 samples are reported as too few to estimate; a missing or unparseable timestamp, or an end earlier than its start, is shown unknown, never zero or negative (LIFE-10, LIFE-7, REQ-cli-020).

Bounded and read-only: transitions are read up to a fixed bound and other records through the existing record bounds, anything beyond a bound is reported partial with what was skipped, and running the report leaves every file under `.chough/` and `.specsync/` byte-identical, runs no case and makes no network request (REQ-cli-006, REQ-cli-020).

docs/cli.md and docs/architecture.md describe the command, the two new transition kinds and the labels; the canonical skill (checkpoint and plan references) tells agents to estimate from `chough timing` ranges and to say when history is too thin, host copies are reinstalled through the known-previous bundle mechanism, and isolated fixtures with fixed timestamps cover every transition kind, gate pairs, missing and out-of-order times, bounds and byte-identical records; the full suite and native structural checks pass on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows CI.

answers.constraints: specs/cli/context.md lessons: list human gates and post-verification steps as plain text, not checkboxes; REQ IDs added by a delta validate only after change check materializes them, so run the scoped check before executing cases for REQ-cli-020; pub(super), not pub(crate); disposable repositories need a local Git identity. Raven triage (issues #10 and #12): Chough writes after change check stale native verification, so the gate record is appended only by the checkpoint command that already writes session.json and adds no new write moment, and .chough/ is not declared as an affected path. Invariants 2, 3, 5, 6 and 8: no approval or review is recorded or inferred, native state is read and never copied, inputs are bounded, unknown stays unknown, and transition history stays append-only. AGENTS.md: Chough owns only its checkpoint, transitions, preferences, cases, observations and bugs, so the gate record extends transitions rather than adding a new store.
